issues.failure_explanation: The theorem statements assume only that A is a continuous injective operator between unspecified Banach spaces, but the existence and convergence proofs explicitly require continuity of A from L2(Ω) (or H1(Ω)) into Y. This hypothesis is neither stated nor implied by the other assumptions, so the proofs do not apply to operators continuous only in a different topology.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: According to \cite{Deng2023,Fleischer1999}, the auto-convolution operator is not injective (e.g.\ $A(f)=A(-f)$). However, when restricted to the cone of strictly nonnegative functions (e.g.\ $f\in C[0,1]$ with $f>0$), $A$ is injective.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem requires A to be injective on the whole space, but auto-convolution satisfies A(f)=A(-f). The example only has injectivity on the cone of nonnegative functions, while the network class X_{n,r} allows negative coefficients a_j and hence sign-changing functions. The iterates are not confined to the cone, so the example does not meet the hypotheses of Theorems 1-2.
